I went without much expectation, but it turned out to be one of the best Japanese-style ramen places I've had—even compared to those in Korea. It’s the most authentic Japanese ramen shop I’ve come across. The cozy, small space gives off the vibe of a local ramen bar in Japan.
Takeout and delivery are not available—you must dine in.

Menu Review:

Tonkotsu Ramen
The broth is rich and savory with deep pork bone flavor. The noodles are fresh and delicious, and the meat is incredibly tender.

Spicy Ramen
Basically the same as the tonkotsu broth, just with spicy chili oil added. Flavor is similar overall.

Mala Ramen
This one really stands out. A mala soup base with grilled meat and fresh noodles—very tasty. If you're into ramen, you must try this place. Highly recommended.

---

Korean:
I went there without much expectations, but it was one of the best Japanese ramen I've had in Korea. This is the exact same store as a real Japanese ramen restaurant. The atmosphere is cozy in a small space, making it feel like a Japanese neighborhood ramen restaurant.
Packaging and delivery are not possible, and only in-person eating is possible.

Menu Rating:

Tonkotsu Ramen
The broth is a really rich and savory beef bone broth. The noodles are really delicious because they are fresh, and the meat is very soft.

Spicy Ramen
It's just tonkotsu ramen broth with spicy chili oil, so the taste is almost the same.

Mara Ramen
This is really special. A combination of spicy meat and raw noodles in malatang soup. Very delicious. If you like ramen, you must come here. Highly recommended.

---

Awalnya saya tidak terlalu berharap, tapi ternyata ini adalah salah satu ramen ala Jepang terenak yang pernah saya coba—bahkan dibandingkan dengan yang ada di Korea. Tempat ini paling mirip dengan kedai ramen Jepang asli. Suasananya hangat dan kecil, seperti kedai ramen di lingkungan Jepang.
Tidak melayani bungkus atau pengantaran—hanya bisa makan di tempat.

Kaldu tulang babinya sangat kaya dan gurih. Mienya buatan sendiri dan sangat enak, dagingnya juga sangat empuk.

The inside is al dente and hard like boiled pasta.

When an order for Jjambbong comes in, only the beef pork belly is grilled and served on top of the pre-made noodles and broth.
It's been a long time since I ate Jjamppong, which was half-cooked without any sincerity.
The store wasn't busy, but the owner could only be seen using his cell phone in the kitchen. I don't know if he was tired of business or just annoyed, but if he's going to make food so half-heartedly, I think he should close the store and just rest at home.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A place with clean Jjajangmyeon~

6-minute walk from Exit 1 of Hoegi Station
This is a Chinese restaurant, and the price of Jjajangmyeon is 7,000 won.

Clean but unfavorable texture
The vegetables and meat in Jjajang are not large in size and have a bit of a chewy taste. Also, the noodles feel a bit undercooked, so the texture is harder than regular black bean noodles. It may be because I ordered it on a deadline, but if it's this style, it may be a factor that can lead to differences in likes and dislikes. What makes it special is that it is cooked in 100% soybean oil rather than pork fat (lard). The overall clean taste stands out, but the lack of the unique savory flavor of pork fat may lead to differing opinions. Still, the occasionally chewy savory taste of sesame seeds is a nice point.

Store & usage tips & overall review
The store is small, but there is a table for two, so you can eat alone. It's quiet after 8 o'clock, so it's good for a quiet meal. It takes a bit of time to cook after ordering.
You order at the table and pay when you leave.
If you order sweet and sour pork by yourself, you have the advantage of being able to eat a mini sweet and sour pork for 10,000 won thanks to a 2,000 won discount when paying in cash. The menu here is simpler than expected, so it has a more professional feel than a typical Chinese restaurant.
Since it only consists of simple menus based on Jjajangmyeon and sweet and sour pork, it may be an advantage for those who find it difficult to choose a menu but want to concentrate and try only a few menu items. If you expect Jjajangmyeon with a large amount of meat or vegetables, it may be a bit boring.

I didn't expect much because I ordered it to cover the cost of the order, but I was satisfied. The burger has a lot of sesame seeds on the bun, so it has a savory taste. The size is just slightly larger than normal. Fresh red onions and wasabi sauce go really well together. The patty is a mixture of whole shrimp and minced shrimp, and the minced ones are also large chunks, so the shrimp texture is preserved well. The menu I would like to personally recommend is the Wasabi Shrimp Burger... The thick and sturdy shrimp patty combined with the wasabi sauce creates an amazing harmony.

The wasabi sauce is not too spicy and has a subtle wasabi taste and aroma. It balances out the greasiness of the shrimp patty well, creating a clean, clean taste. It also offers a new taste that you haven't experienced anywhere else.

The cheeseburger is also great, with the juicy beef patty, fresh vegetables, and the restaurant's unique sauce going well together for a great taste.

It is said that the buns for all burgers are ordered separately and used specifically for the Hoegi Burger...

I would like to recommend this place to those who are tired of the typical taste of large franchise hamburgers, so if you have the chance, please visit this place.

A house specializing in hamburgers
Located a 7-minute walk from Exit 1 of Hoegi Station.
The basic hamburger costs 12,500 won.
​
Visual good~
It is the most diverse among the hamburgers I have seen.
It feels fancy with french fries as a topping.
Hamburger consists of French fries, fried egg, and bean sprouts.
It comes as a set with salad, kimchi, pickled radish, rice, and soup.
The cabbage salad had a slightly rough texture, but I was satisfied with the sesame sauce, which I like.
The hamburger is served with demi-glace sauce, and it tastes like the sauce you usually get in Japan.
So, for someone like me who likes umami, it's a disappointing taste.
Still, if you like this style, it's good enough~
The hamburger is thick and has a good texture.
Overall, it is a well-organized hamburger house.
To compare, I recently ate hamburger at Gyeongdong Market.
If you want a thick sauce, refreshing hamburger may be better~
​
Store & Tips & Review

There are many tables for two, so you can easily eat alone.
You can order using the QR provided on the table, but
